subject: Files
notes: SHARING WITH READ ONLY, AGAINST OTHER RUN UNITS (kb/Work PB833 landed). cite.py --check 9.1.15 'The successful opening of a file establishes a file lock for the applicable sharing rules, thereby preventing other run units from opening that file with incompatible sharing rules' -> OK 9.1.15 3); cite.py --check 9.1.15 'restricts concurrent access to a physical file through file connectors other than this one, to input mode' -> OK 9.1.15 2); cite.py --check 9.1.13.9 'A file sharing conflict condition exists because an OPEN statement is attempted on a physical file' -> OK 9.1.13.9 1); cite.py --check 14.9.27.4 'If the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful, the file is not affected' -> OK 14.9.27.4 25). MEASURED BEFORE: tests/WiseOwl.Cobol.Tests.Unit/RunUnitFileLockDriftTests (a second FileRegistry is a second run unit: it shares neither the PhysicalFileTable nor a host handle with the first) failed 15 of 768 pairs on Windows (every OPEN OUTPUT against an ALL OTHER holder and RO/OUTPUT against ALL OTHER INPUT answered 00 and truncated the file, where Table 19 prints Unsuccessful open in every OUTPUT cell: a host share mode refuses by ACCESS and a sibling's posture admits the writer) and, on Linux, every pair whose refusal needs a share mode that admits a reader and refuses a writer (.NET maps every FileShare but None onto one flock LOCK_SH). FIX: the ONE cross-run-unit verdict is Table19.Cell. FileConnector.Open takes RunUnitFileLock before OpenCore on an existing file (after the body on one it created): the OPEN publishes its Table 19 column (Table19.Column) as a SHARED open-file-description region lock (fcntl F_OFD_SETLK) on one byte at 2^62 + the column's wire number and tests, with F_OFD_GETLK, the columns its request row refuses (Table19.Cell == UnsuccessfulOpen) for another holder; a holder is refused with 61 (9.1.13.9 1)) and the file is untouched (14.9.27.4 GR25). Publish-first makes two simultaneous OPENs unable to both pass; F_OFD_GETLK ignores the asker's own description, so classes that refuse their own kind (NO OTHER, OUTPUT) do not refuse themselves. The lock is unlocked and closed by the CLOSE (9.1.15: 'The file lock is removed by an explicit or implicit CLOSE statement') and by an unsuccessful OPEN, and dies with a terminated run unit. OPEN OUTPUT on an existing file also asks the host for exclusive access first (HostFile.IsHeldByAnother) on EVERY host, which is what closed the Windows gap. NOW: RunUnitFileLockDriftTests.ASecondRunUnitsOpenIsArbitratedByTable19 passes all 768 (spelling x mode x spelling x mode x organization) pairs on Windows and in the Linux clone (WSL, scripts/linux-gate.sh), TheCloseGivesTheFileLockBack proves the give-back for all three organizations, TwoSimultaneousExclusiveOpens_NeverBothSucceed runs 200 barrier-released rounds. CAPABILITY IS MEASURED, NOT SWITCHED ON A PLATFORM: OfdRegionLocks.Open answers null (Take: Unavailable) for an ABI it was not written for, a missing libc (Windows, where FileShare already carries the table plus the OUTPUT probe), EINVAL (no OFD locks) or ENOLCK/EOPNOTSUPP (a filesystem without byte-range locks). JUDGMENT FOR THE REFUTER: macOS is Unavailable (no CI leg runs it; its process-owned fcntl locks drop when any descriptor closes, and its OFD commands are unconfirmed private ones), so rule 2 is not refused across run units there; docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-75 and DESIGN-runtime-library.md say so, and the row is CONFORMS for the hosts the project builds and tests (Windows, Linux). A non-COBOL process that takes no lock meets only the share mode (Annex A.1 item 75). Rules 1) and 3) were CONFORMS and remain so: rule 1 is FileShare.None plus the NoOtherAnyMode column, rule 3 refuses nothing. The in-run-unit half (Table 19 via the PhysicalFileTable) was already CONFORMS. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/Sharing/OfdRegionLocks.cs#HoldShared (kb/Work PB2660 generalized HoldShared into Hold(exclusive, wait); RunUnitFileLock calls it with exclusive: false) || kb/Work PB1587 (w1126c): the INPUT connector rule 2) admits beside a READ ONLY writer READS every record that writer released (pb1587_write_released_to_input_reader legs A-D), and a READ ONLY reader beside it is refused '61' with the writer unaffected (leg E; ARefusedReader_Is61_AndTheWriterIsUnaffected).
